questions.q: Which is an example of a software interrupt?
options: A printer runs out of paper
A program tries to divide by zero
questions.why: Program errors such as division by zero are software interrupts. The others come from hardware.

questions.q: When does the CPU check for interrupts?
options: Only when the user presses a key
At the end of each fetch–decode–execute cycle
At the start of the program
questions.why: The CPU checks at the end of each FDE cycle and handles the interrupt if its priority is high enough.

questions.q: Which translator converts assembly language into machine code?
questions.why: An assembler translates assembly language. Compilers and interpreters translate high-level languages.

questions.q: Give two differences between a compiler and an interpreter.
questions.model: A compiler translates the whole program at once into an executable file, but an interpreter translates and runs one line at a time. A compiled program runs faster and does not need the compiler to run, but an interpreter stops at the first error.
points: compiler translates all at once, interpreter line by line
one other valid difference (speed, errors, executable, source code)
